claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or patterned nanoribbons are nanocrystalline.
These as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type materials have a high interfacial grain-boundary density.
These as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type materials contain significant local lattice strain.
Nanoscale structural disorder and interfacial strain govern the low-field magnetocaloric response and associated hysteresis.
Structural disorder and interfacial strain modify magnetic-domain-wall mobility and phase-transition kinetics.
Local lattice distortions and grain boundaries create spatial variations in magnetic exchange interactions.
Local lattice distortions and grain boundaries impede coherent domain-wall motion.
Impaired domain-wall motion and heterogeneous exchange interactions broaden the magnetic transition and produce pronounced magnetocaloric hysteresis.
Moderate post-deposition annealing below the onset of grain growth will relax interfacial strain and reduce local disorder without significant nanostructural coarsening.
Annealing-induced defect reduction will facilitate a sharper magnetic phase transition.
Annealed samples will have a narrower magnetic hysteresis loop than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will show a steeper and more pronounced isothermal entropy-change response than as-deposited samples under low applied fields.
The as-deposited baseline has a muted magnetocaloric effect and broad hysteresis because of interfacial strain and disorder.
The hypothesis applies to films thinner than 100 nm or similarly scaled nanoribbons.
The proposed behavior applies under magnetic fields below approximately 100 mT and at temperatures near the alloy's Curie point.
Heat-transfer constraints limit the usable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Behavior in bulk forms may differ from behavior in nanoscale films and nanoribbons.
Grain-boundary density and interfacial strain are documented as influential in other high-entropy-alloy properties such as radiation resistance.

Failure of annealing to produce both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and an enhanced magnetocaloric transition under the defined conditions would falsify the claim that disorder and strain are dominant governing factors.
